scope: Source and documentation review; no native processor/GUI runtime executed

inspected_existing_programs.name: Harp
inspected_existing_programs.description: A finger-plucked harp string excites a rounded soundboard response with a broad, softly notched upper spectrum. The short contact rank shares the string's pitch, then yields to a long lower aftersound. Soft arpeggios retain their gentler attack and can ring across key releases.

inspected_existing_programs.name: Koto
inspected_existing_programs.description: A near-bridge plectrum opens a bright notched string spectrum over the koto's long-board response. A quiet short contact rank shares the played pitch; upper string modes soften before the ringing body. Restrained initial settling leaves the ribbon available for deliberate bends.

inspected_existing_programs.name: Banjo
inspected_existing_programs.description: A sharp string pluck excites the banjo's membrane-and-bridge response, with a strong low-mid body and a dry bright edge. Fast losses around the head resonance let the sound clear between picked notes; the brief contact rank adds no unrelated clavichord or held oscillator buzz.

inspected_existing_programs.name: Kalimba
inspected_existing_programs.description: A thumb-plucked supported tine gives a rounded fundamental and a brief nonharmonic ping, distinct from an electric-piano pickup. Both ranks share the played pitch; the brighter contact fades first while the lower tine continues ringing after key release.

inspected_existing_programs.name: Tubular Bells
inspected_existing_programs.description: A struck tube carries a weak low spectrum and a bright octave nominal, with the near 2:3:4 upper group suggesting the played pitch. The separate hard contact shares the same tube tuning, then clears to leave its independently decaying metal modes.

inspected_existing_programs.name: Music Box
inspected_existing_programs.description: A small plucked comb tooth rings with a clear high pitch and sparse upper resonances near 6.27 times its fundamental. A short same-pitch contact glint lights the attack; the bright overtones fade into the simple mechanical ringing tail.

inspected_existing_programs.name: Gong
inspected_existing_programs.description: A low mallet thud opens into a dense, irregular set of plate modes. Delayed upper resonances bloom after the impact, then lose energy at different rates; the same tuned plate supplies the strike and the lingering, shifting aftersound.

inspected_existing_programs.name: Temple Bell
inspected_existing_programs.description: A deep struck shell rings with stable close mode pairs and slow metallic beating. Widely separated upper resonances recede from the initial clang, leaving a calm low aftersound; the brief hard contact and the long body share one shell pitch.

inspected_existing_programs.name: Agogo
inspected_existing_programs.description: A small hollow bell opens with a hard contact and several widely spaced metal resonances. Its compact shell damps quickly for repeated strokes; a short same-pitch upper knock adds definition to each crisp metal hit.
